free_tier.stated: Every workspace starts on Starter at USD 0 with USD 100 in free credits on first adding a payment method; Starter allows 5 concurrent sessions and machines up to 4 cores / 8 GB.
free_tier.notes: The USD 100 is one-time and requires a payment method: Stripe verifies the card with a USD 0 authorization before granting it. The free Starter plan also exists without the credit once the balance runs out.

per_object_cap.stated: The unit is a VM, not an object. The default Small sandbox is 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 5 GiB root disk; the Starter plan caps machines at 4 cores / 8 GB RAM and storage at 100 GiB per workspace.

retention.stated: A sandbox can be paused and resumed with its files and memory kept for later; storage on Starter is 100 GiB per workspace with snapshots, volumes and sticky disks drawing from that pool.

egress.terms: No egress allowance or price per TB is stated on the pricing page; storage is priced at USD 0.20 per GiB per month from the first byte and serving the runner cache is included in the runner rate.

record.interface_detail: A CLI installed from luxor.ai/install.sh with luxor onboard, plus Go, TypeScript and Python SDKs; sandbox sessions expose command execution, file I/O, preview URLs and SSH.
record.tooling: luxor CLI (curl -fsSL https://luxor.ai/install.sh | sh), npm @luxorai/sandbox, go.luxor.ai/sandbox and pip luxor-ai SDKs.
record.chaining: A sandbox can expose a preview URL and mount a workspace volume, so a coding agent can run a service and keep its files between sessions within the same workspace credit pool.

limits.value: USD 100 one-time free credits on adding a payment method; sandbox vCPU USD 0.000014 per second, memory USD 0.0000045 per GiB-second and disk USD 0.00000003 per GiB-second with 5 GiB free
Starter: 5 concurrent sessions, 4 cores / 8 GB machine limit, 100 GiB storage and 5 members per workspace
the USD 100 credit is granted only after adding a card or Link wallet, and each new CLI key needs a device approval click in the browser

record.limits_note: Billing is per second of active session time; paused sandboxes stop charging and keep files and memory. When the balance runs out, the platform stops starting new sessions until a top-up of at least USD 20 or auto-reload.
record.binding_note: The USD 100 one-time credit is the first constraint to run out at sustained use; the Starter five-session and 4-core caps are plan limits, and a card is required before the credit even exists.

identity_cost.detail: The free credits page states that after creating an account you add a card or Link wallet from the Billing tab and Stripe verifies it with a USD 0 authorization before the one-time USD 100 credit is granted; the onboarding docs say sign-in or registration is at app.luxor.ai/auth/registration with Google or GitHub, and CLI login requires a browser device approval click. No phone or ID document is stated.

record.reliability_note: When credits run out, Luxor Agent Cloud stops starting new jobs and sessions until the workspace is topped up by at least USD 20 or auto-reload is enabled; an unpaid invoice interrupts service and cancels running jobs.
record.confidence_note: Plan limits, per-second rates, the card-gated credit and the sign-in flow are quoted from vendor pricing, free-credits and onboarding pages read on 2026-11-25.

record.notes: Luxor Agent Cloud (formerly Tenki) sells disposable Linux VM sandboxes, GitHub Actions runners and a code reviewer from one workspace balance. The default Small sandbox is 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 5 GiB at USD 0.17 per running hour from the per-second rate card, and the free Starter plan allows 5 concurrent sessions with a USD 100 one-time credit that requires adding a card. A paid Team plan raises the limits but does not change the per-second rates. The card requirement to unlock the free credit, and the USD 20 minimum top-up when the balance runs out, are the caveats.

card.summary: USD 100 one-time credit when a payment method is added; Starter plan is USD 0 plus usage beyond the credit

free_tier.stated: USD 100 one-time credit when a payment method is added; Starter plan is USD 0 plus usage beyond the credit
free_tier.notes: The credit is released only after a card or Link wallet passes a USD 0 authorization; no card means no credit. Credits are spent at the standard per-unit rates.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a virtual machine, not an object store; the first 5 GiB of sandbox disk is included

retention.stated: A paused sandbox keeps its files and memory; a non-sticky session is paused automatically at its maximum duration; disks are wiped on teardown; persistent volumes and snapshots are managed separately.

egress.terms: not published: the pricing rate card lists vCPU, memory, disk and storage with no outbound transfer allowance or per-GB price; the sandbox page states 'Tunneled, authenticated connections. No public IPs.'

record.interface_detail: The `luxor` CLI and Go, TypeScript and Python SDKs against https://api.luxor.ai; the sandbox CLI reference documents port exposure and SSH into a session. No public IP is assigned.
record.tooling: curl -fsSL https://luxor.ai/install.sh | sh installs the CLI; SDKs are npm install @luxorai/sandbox, pip install luxor-ai and go get go.luxor.ai/sandbox.
record.chaining: Creates isolated full Linux VMs for agent tasks with snapshots and persistent volumes; hosted only, with no user-owned hardware involved.

limits.value: Starter caps a machine at 4 cores / 8 GB RAM, 5 concurrent sessions and 100 GiB of workspace storage; raises to 16 cores / 64 GB, 100 sessions and 1,000 GiB on Team
at the concurrency limit a job queues rather than fails; a Starter job targeting a larger size is blocked rather than queued
when the workspace has no usable credit, new jobs and sessions are rejected until a top-up of at least $20 or auto-reload

record.limits_note: Sandbox rates beyond the credit are $0.00084 per vCPU-minute, $0.00027 per GiB-minute, $0.0000018 per GiB-minute of disk after the first 5 GiB, and $0.20 per GiB-month of storage from the first byte. Billing is per second with no minimums.
record.binding_note: The USD 100 credit and the Starter machine ceiling bind first: credit covers roughly 25,000 minutes on a 2 vCPU runner and a larger Starter size is blocked until a payment method is on file.

identity_cost.detail: Registration starts GitHub sign-up at app.luxor.ai/auth/registration; the USD 100 credit requires adding a card or Link wallet from the Billing tab, and Stripe verifies it with a USD 0 authorization. The registration page itself shows no separate email, phone or ID gate.

record.reliability_note: SSD disks are mounted from Ceph; a sandbox is not paused for inactivity, so a running session accrues charges until paused or terminated; jobs are balance-gated and stop starting when credit runs out. Auto-reload adds $20 when the balance drops below $5.
record.confidence_note: The credit gate, per-second rates, plan ceilings, card check, concurrency and no-public-IP statement are quoted from first-party pages read on 2026-11-24.
